items.title: SL-0981 reaches its nine-month limit on 20 October
items.line: Put the delay on record with ICICI before the limit passes. The letter is ready.
items.why_now: Export money is due within nine months of the invoice date, and an exporter still unpaid a year past that can be restricted to advance payment only. SL-0981 is dated 20 January 2026, so the limit is 20 October 2026.
facts: Invoice SL-0981, pitch deck design, $1,200, dated 20 Jan 2026, is still unpaid.
On 30 Sep, Copperline's accounts team wrote that it is scheduled for their November payment run.

RBI: export proceeds are due within nine months; the bank can extend the time when the exporter asks with reasons. Unpaid a year past the due date, the exporter may only export against advance payment or a letter of credit.

The invoice predates the 1 October export-form regime, so ICICI holds no declaration for it. The letter asks the bank to record the expected date, so the money can be received and matched without question when it arrives.
steps: Clock: 8 days to the nine-month limit.
Reminding Copperline to pay is the RazorpayX Receivables Agent's job, so Homeward does not chase them. Homeward handles the bank side.
Drafted a request to ICICI to record an extension to 31 Dec 2026, using the reason in Copperline's email of 30 Sep.
items.baseline: A fixed rule can flag the date. It cannot find the reason in the client's email or write the request.
prepared: Extension request letter to ICICI's trade desk, with Copperline's email of 30 Sep attached. You decide whether to send it; some banks will only note it.
